title: Adaptive cache coherency and metadata shimming playbook
author: Marisol Ortega
content:
Summary:

This playbook documents the design, operational procedures, and testing guidance for our adaptive cache coherency and metadata shimming layer (service name: platform-kv-shim). The shim is responsible for keeping per-tenant KV prefix caches consistent across redis/gcache pools and for emitting metadata that enables safe partial eviction, hot-key protection, and graceful degradation for latency-sensitive inference requests.

Audience:
- Platform engineers operating GPU-backed inference pools
- SREs maintaining cache clusters and autoscaling policies
- Runtime engineers implementing batching and KV cache hooks

Goals and success criteria:
- Maintain 99.95% cache-hit-awareness (see instrumentation below) for 99th-percentile token latency SLOs
- Reduce unnecessary cache invalidation events by >= 40% in mixed-tenant traces
- Provide safe fallback behavior that keeps tail-latency below 300ms for foreground requests during cache inconsistency windows

Motivation and scope:
- Problem: multi-tenant KV/prefix caches can diverge after shard failover, network partitions, or aggressive eviction. Divergence causes inference token spikes as runtimes rehydrate KV caches synchronously, creating cascading latency and higher cost.
- Scope: this document covers the shim component that normalizes metadata across stores, the operational runbook for incidents, and simulation/gameday steps for validating behavior pre-rollout. It does NOT cover kernel-level scheduling (see eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling).

Key concepts and terminology:
- platform-kv-shim: stateless service that tracks metadata (version, last-write, hot-score) and mediates cache change broadcasts
- prefix-cache: per-tenant per-model KV entries used to speed autoregressive generation
- hot-score: exponentially-weighted metric (1m/5m) used to protect or throttle entries during bursts
- coherency-token: short-lived signed token used by runtimes to assert cache freshness

Design overview:
1) Metadata shimming: platform-kv-shim subscribes to change feeds from primary stores (redis-main, gcache-cluster). On write, it records a compact metadata row in the shim-store and emits a change event to the mesh. Runtimes fetch metadata-only before expensive KV rehydrate operations.

2) Adaptive coherency policy: based on last-write age, hot-score, and tenant-priority, the shim decides:
- full-invalidate (force rehydrate)
- lazy-validate (check a small sample before full rehydrate)
- optimistic-use (use local cache with background revalidate)

3) Fallback safety nets: shim includes guard rails:
- synchronous fallback for foreground requests when coherency-token expired and request latency budget allows
- canary toggles per-tenant for new policies

Operational playbook (incident handling):
- Symptoms to watch for:
  - Sudden increase in token-generation latency (p50->p99 delta >100ms) with cache-miss burst
  - Elevated rehydrate QPS to redis-main (>60% sustained of baseline)
  - spike in platform-kv-shim change-event errors (>=1% error-rate)

- Immediate mitigation steps (ordered):
  1) Move impacted tenant(s) to optimistic-use mode via the shim feature-flag endpoint. CLI:
     ```bash
     curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP" -d '{"tenant":"tenant-id","mode":"optimistic"}' https://platform-kv-shim.$REGION.internal/api/v1/flags
     ```
  2) Increase shard read capacity: scale gcache-cluster read_replicas by +2 in the region. Terraform snippet: see rollout table.
  3) If rehydration storm persists, trigger tenant-level soft-throttle: apply token-based rate-limit in traffic-shepherd for the tenant routing key.

- Owners and escalation:
  - First responder: platform-cache-ops (pager)
  - Escalate (15m) to runtime-oncall if rehydrate QPS > 2x baseline
  - Executive notify if incident predicted to exceed 1 hour or affects >5% of production tenants

Runbook steps for controlled rollback:
1) Disable new coherency policy: set POLICY_VERSION=stable on platform-kv-shim via console.
2) Re-enable synchronous coherent-writes on redis-main for the impacted shards for 10 minutes to re-seed metadata.
3) Validate: cause small synthetic regeneration (see Simulation section) and verify p99 latency is back within SLOs.

Configuration and thresholds (table):
| config_key | default | safe_range | notes |
|-----------|---------:|-----------:|-------|
| coherency_token_ttl_seconds | 30 | 10-300 | Shorter TTL reduces stale-reads but increases token churn |
| hot_score_threshold | 0.7 | 0.5-0.95 | Threshold above which item is hot-protected (less likely to evict) |
| lazy_validate_sample_size | 3 | 1-10 | Checked keys before committing to full rehydrate |
| rehydrate_surge_qps_ratio | 1.5 | 1.2-2.0 | Surge over baseline to trigger mitigation |

Instrumentation and dashboards to monitor (Dashboards and Alerts):
- Dashboard: KV Shim Overview (grafana id: redwood.graf.kv_shim.overview)
  - panels: coherency-token-age histogram, rehydrate-qps by tenant, hot-score distribution, shim-event-errors
- Alerts (recommended):
  - KV_REHYDRATE_SPIKE: rehydrate_qps / baseline > 1.5 for 5m -> Severity: P2, notify platform-cache-ops
  - SHIM_EVENT_ERRORS_HIGH: shim_event_error_rate > 0.5% for 10m -> Severity: P1, notify runtime-oncall
  - TOKEN_EXPIRY_SPIKE: coherency_token_ttl_exceeded_count > 1000/min -> Severity: P2

Simulation and gameday plan (pre-rollout validation):
1) Synthetic workload generator: use platform-loadgen with these parameters to emulate mixed tenants:
   - 2000 foreground requests/min, mix ratio 70:30 foreground:background, skewed hot keys for 10% of tenants.
2) Failure killsets to test:
   - shard failover (kill one redis-main instance)
   - network partition (delay 200ms between shim and gcache)
   - eviction storm (simulate memory pressure causing 20% eviction)
3) Success criteria during simulation:
   - p99 token latency remains < 300ms for foreground requests
   - rehydrate QPS surge contained within rehydrate_surge_qps_ratio threshold
   - no more than 2% of requests return degraded/soft-fallback responses

Rollout plan (canary approach):
1) Unit testing + integration tests in staging with platform-loadgen and CI coverage >= 95% for metadata logic.
2) Canary: enable adaptive coherency for 5 low-traffic tenants for 48 hours. Monitor dashboards and run daily sanity checks.
3) Incrementally increase to 20 tenants, then to 200 after 72 hours with automated rollback on alert thresholds.

Safe config snippets (terraform / curl):
- Example feature-flag enable (curl):
  ```bash
  curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/flags \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \n    -d '{"name":"adaptive-coherency-enabled","value":true,"scope":"region-us-west-2"}'
  ```
- Example terraform snippet to add read replicas:
  ```hcl
  resource "gcache_cluster_replica" "extra_read" {
    count = 2
    cluster_id = module.gcache.cluster_id
    instance_type = "r5.large"
    region = var.region
  }
  ```

Post-incident retrospective checklist (retrospectives):
- Within 48 hours: capture timeline, decision log, and mitigation commands executed in the incident ticket.
- Within 7 days: run a targeted simulation that reproduces the incident and validate the proposed code/hardening fixes.
- Within 30 days: schedule a cross-team retro with runtime, platform, and SRE to adjust SLAs, dashboards, or defaults if needed.

Appendix A — example observability query (promql):
- Rehydrate QPS per tenant:
  rate(platform_kv_rehydrate_calls_total{tenant!~"test.*"}[5m])

Appendix B — ownership and contacts:
- Service owner: platform-cache-team@example.redwood.com (primary), oncall: platform-cache-ops pager
- Runtime integration owner: runtime-team@example.redwood.com
- SRE escalation: sre-oncall@example.redwood.com

End of playbook.
